sections.title: Warm-up
sections.prompt: Think of the last email you sent. What was the subject line and the first sentence?
sections.lede: Say each line aloud once. This section is not scored.

sections.title: Learning objectives
sections.lede: These are the three things you will be able to do by the end of the lesson.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: A German email has a clear subject, a correct salutation, a focused request and a matching closing.

blocks.text: The subject line should be short and specific: “Frage zu meiner Bestellung” is better than “Hallo”. In a formal email, the salutation uses “Sehr geehrte/r” plus surname, or “Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren” if you do not know the name.

Structure the body in three moves: context, request and closing. Give the reader the information they need, ask one clear question, and end with a formula such as “Mit freundlichen Grüßen”. Informal emails can be shorter and warmer, but they still benefit from a clear subject.

blocks.title: One email, one purpose
blocks.text: If you have two unrelated requests, send two emails. A single clear request is more likely to get a quick answer.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: The patterns to keep in mind while you work through the examples.

items: After the formal salutation, continue with a lower-case word on the next line.
Put the most important request in its own short paragraph.
Use “Vielen Dank im Voraus” only when you expect a reply.

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.lede: Listen once, then read the example aloud.

items.example: Der Betreff sollte kurz und klar sein.
items.exampleEn: The subject line should be short and clear.

items.example: Die Anrede steht am Anfang der E-Mail.
items.exampleEn: The salutation stands at the beginning of the email.

items.example: Ich habe eine Bitte: Können Sie mir helfen?
items.exampleEn: I have a request: can you help me?

sections.title: Example sentences
sections.lede: Notice how the pattern behaves in a complete sentence.

items.note: A specific subject helps the reader act.

items.de: Sehr geehrte Frau Weber, ich schreibe Ihnen wegen meiner Bestellung.
items.en: Dear Ms Weber, I am writing to you about my order.
items.note: Ihnen is the formal dative pronoun.

items.de: Könnten Sie mir bitte die Lieferzeit mitteilen?
items.en: Could you please let me know the delivery time?
items.note: One clear request in a polite form.

items.de: Vielen Dank im Voraus. Mit freundlichen Grüßen, Ali Yildiz
items.en: Thank you in advance. Kind regards, Ali Yildiz

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Short, focused sound work. Play each item and repeat it twice.

items.hint: Stress the second syllable: be-TREF. The final ff is short.

blocks.text: German business email tends to be direct but polite. Get to the point after one short opening sentence; long warm-up paragraphs can feel inefficient.
Formality is often higher than in English-language email. Using a first name without an invitation can feel intrusive, especially with older colleagues or officials.

sections.title: Dialogue in context
sections.lede: Read the scene, then play it and follow the speakers.
sections.setting: A customer writes to a shop about a delayed order.

lines.speaker: E-Mail
lines.de: Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren, ich habe am Montag eine Jacke bestellt.
lines.en: Dear Sir or Madam, I ordered a jacket on Monday.

lines.speaker: E-Mail
lines.de: Leider ist die Lieferung noch nicht angekommen. Könnten Sie mir bitte den Status mitteilen?
lines.en: Unfortunately the delivery has not arrived yet. Could you please tell me the status?

lines.speaker: E-Mail
lines.de: Vielen Dank im Voraus. Mit freundlichen Grüßen, Sara Klein
lines.en: Thank you in advance. Kind regards, Sara Klein

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: The anatomy of an email
sections.lede: Each part has a standard phrase you can reuse.

blocks.text: In informal emails, “Hallo Jonas” and “Liebe Grüße” are enough. In formal email, keep the full salutation and closing even if the message is short.

sections.tip: Write the subject line last. Once you know your request, you can summarise it in three or four words.

sections.title: Choose the right answer
sections.lede: Choose the answer that fits the sentence or the rule.

exercises.prompt: Which subject line is most appropriate for a formal email?
exercises.explanation: A specific subject line tells the reader what the email is about.

exercises.prompt: Sehr geehrte Frau Weber, ___ schreibe Ihnen wegen meiner Bestellung.
exercises.explanation: The subject pronoun ich follows the salutation.
Mit freundlichen Grüßen is the standard formal closing.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence makes a polite request?
options: Könnten Sie mir das bitte schicken?
exercises.explanation: Könnten Sie … bitte is the polite formal request pattern.

sections.title: Complete the sentence
sections.lede: Type the missing word or ending. Spelling counts.

exercises.explanation: The formal salutation begins with Sehr geehrte.
The closing formula ends with Grüßen.
Wegen introduces the reason for writing.

exercises.prompt: Könnten Sie mir bitte den Status ___?
exercises.explanation: Mitteilen means to inform or let someone know.

sections.title: Build the sentence
sections.lede: Click the words in the order that makes a correct German sentence.

exercises.prompt: Build: “I am writing to you about my order.”
exercises.answer: Ich schreibe Ihnen wegen meiner Bestellung.
exercises.explanation: Ihnen is the formal dative object, followed by the reason.

exercises.prompt: Build: “Could you please let me know the delivery time?”
exercises.answer: Könnten Sie mir die Lieferzeit mitteilen?
exercises.explanation: The modal opens the question and the infinitive closes it.
This is a fixed formal phrase.

sections.title: Listening
sections.lede: Listen twice before you look at the transcript.
sections.speaker: Eine E-Mail wird vorgelesen

script.speaker: Sekretärin
script.de: Sehr geehrter Herr Braun, leider muss ich unseren Termin verschieben.
script.en: Dear Mr Braun, unfortunately I have to move our appointment.

script.speaker: Sekretärin
script.de: Könnten Sie mir bitte mitteilen, ob Ihnen Montag um zehn Uhr passt?
script.en: Could you please let me know whether Monday at ten suits you?

questions.explanation: The writer says she has to move the appointment.

questions.prompt: What does she ask Mr Braun?
options: Whether Monday at ten suits him
questions.explanation: She asks whether Monday at ten is convenient.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Record or say your answer aloud, then compare it with the model.
sections.prompt: Draft and say a short formal email: subject, greeting, reason, request and closing.

model.de: Betreff: Frage zu meinem Kurs. Sehr geehrte Frau Weber, ich schreibe Ihnen wegen meines Kurses. Könnten Sie mir bitte den neuen Termin mitteilen? Vielen Dank. Mit freundlichen Grüßen, Ali Yildiz.
model.en: Subject: Question about my course. Dear Ms Weber, I am writing to you about my course. Could you please let me know the new date? Thank you. Kind regards, Ali Yildiz.

tips: Say the subject line first, as if you were reading the email aloud.
Keep the request to one sentence.
Use the same formal closing every time so it becomes automatic.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: These are the errors learners most often make with this pattern.

items.why: A subject line should state the topic, not greet the reader.

items.wrong: Sehr geehrte Frau Weber, Ich schreibe Ihnen …
items.right: Sehr geehrte Frau Weber, ich schreibe Ihnen …
items.why: After the salutation comma, the next word is lower case.
The fixed closing uses the dative plural Grüßen.
